options.why_wrong: A participle phrase on its own cannot serve as the main clause, so the sentence remains a fragment.

options.text: the department began hiring new staff.

options.why_wrong: An infinitive phrase has no subject and no finite verb, so it cannot complete the main clause.

options.text: since the department began hiring new staff.
options.why_wrong: 'Since' adds a second subordinator after the absolute phrase, so the sentence has no main clause.

grammar_focus: Absolute phrases with a noun and past participle, followed by a main clause
explanation: The opening 'with' phrase is an absolute structure: a noun followed by a past participle that adds background to the main clause. The main clause must then have its own subject and finite verb. Polish speakers may add a second connector or leave out the main clause, because Polish often expresses the same background with a full subordinate clause.
